verdict.justification: B is the more effective assessor briefing: it follows the requested nine-slide structure and summarises progress, spending, risks and next steps without the excessive detail in A. Both report the key financial position correctly—£10,298.70 spent against £9,874.37 profiled—but B's grouped cost categories and clearly defined variance convention are better suited to a monthly presentation. A adds a large resource-utilisation table and extensive workbook commentary, making its progress and spending slides substantially less concise than requested. A also overstates the evidence when it says the architecture was “acceptance-tested on 15 Oct”; the log records planned acceptance testing and subsequent feedback, not explicit confirmation that acceptance testing was completed. A deserves credit for identifying the conflicting 7 and 9 November Output 1 dates and proposing an assessor discussion, which B does not explicitly address. B nevertheless needs a chronology correction: “Review 2 was held 3 Nov” describes a future event as completed in a report dated 30 October.
